title: Mastering the Copy Button UX
summary: This reel outlines five essential best practices for designing copy-to-clipboard buttons. It covers instant feedback, state resets, data integrity, accessibility, and error handling for insecure origins.

transcript.text: One click, one checkmark. You pasted absolutely nothing.
The copy icon should flip to a check the instant the copy fires. No spinner, no delay.
Hold the check for about two seconds, then let it fade back to the copy icon. Leave it stuck forever and the next copy gives no signal at all.
Copy the raw value, not the formatted span with its line breaks and hidden zero-width characters. Paste that into a terminal. Watch it break.
Screen readers hear nothing when an icon quietly changes. Announce "copied" out loud through a live region, because silent success is still a failure for someone.
On an insecure origin, the clipboard call fails without a word. Fall back to a copy command. A silent button lies.
Copy needs proof. Go to designmotionhq.com for more. Link in bio.

on_screen_text: INSTANT FEEDBACK: Flip the instant it fires.
AUTO RESET: Hold, then fade back.
CLEAN VALUE: Copy the raw value.
SCREEN READERS: Say it out loud.
INSECURE ORIGIN: Fall back, don't lie.
design_principles: Instant Feedback: Avoid spinners for instantaneous actions like copying.
State Reset: Revert success icons to their original state after a short delay (e.g., 2 seconds).
Data Integrity: Ensure the clipboard receives raw data rather than formatted text that might include hidden characters.
Accessibility: Use aria-live to announce state changes to screen reader users.
Graceful Degradation: Provide fallbacks for API failures on insecure origins.
before_after: Demonstrates the difference between a basic, often broken copy button and a robust, accessible implementation.
